passage: Sonali, you used to laugh at my blue folder. "Damini the filing queen," you said. Well, last Tuesday an email arrived at four saying the new job's form needed my ID, degree certificate, address proof and last year's tax receipt by six. I didn't panic. I opened the blue folder: everything in plastic sleeves, in the same order as the checklist I keep inside the cover. Then I opened the scans on my laptop, named by document, and attached them. Eleven minutes. The colleague at the next desk was still hunting for a marksheet in a cupboard when I pressed send. Every new receipt takes thirty seconds to slot in. That's the whole trick. Come on Sunday and I'll help you set yours up.

qa.q: What four things did the form need by six o'clock?
qa.a: It needed Damini's ID, degree certificate, address proof and last year's tax receipt.

qa.q: How did Damini feel when the email arrived at four?
qa.a: Calm and unworried, because everything was already in the blue folder and on the laptop.

qa.q: What everyday habit made the eleven-minute submission possible?
qa.a: Slotting each new receipt into the folder right away, and keeping named scans on the laptop.

qa.q: Why was the colleague's afternoon more stressful than Damini's?
qa.a: The colleague was still hunting for a marksheet in a cupboard while Damini had everything organised and had already sent the form.

grounding: Shows a prepared person whose folder of originals and one set of scans makes an urgent form easy.

passage: I'm Harsha, and I live next door to Neelam. Last month her phone rang at nine at night: the passport appointment had moved to the next morning. I braced for a panic. Instead she took a green folder off the shelf, checked a list inside the cover, and laid out the originals: ID, address proof, two photographs, the old passport. Then she opened her laptop and showed me a scan of each in one folder. Fifteen minutes later she was making tea. "Every paper goes in the day I get it," she said. Meanwhile mine are spread over three drawers and a shoebox. I looked at that folder longer than I meant to.

qa.q: What time did Neelam's phone ring?
qa.a: It rang at nine at night.

qa.q: What was Neelam feeling as she laid out her documents?
qa.a: Calm and in control, judging from the fact that she was making tea fifteen minutes later.

qa.q: What could Harsha do this weekend after seeing Neelam's method?
qa.a: Gather the papers into one folder with a checklist, scan each one, and add new papers the day they arrive.

qa.q: What might Harsha have been thinking while looking at the green folder for so long?
qa.a: Harsha probably felt a little envious and embarrassed, since Harsha's own papers are in three drawers and a shoebox. 🙂

grounding: Shows a neighbour watching someone with organised originals and scans handle an urgent document request calmly.
